Nuremberg Synagogue (Arno-Hamburger-Straße)

Synagogue · Nürnberg, Germany

The synagogue at what is now Arno-Hamburger-Straße 1 in Nuremberg was inaugurated on 8 September 1984, exactly 110 years after the dedication of the city's earlier Grand Synagogue at Hans-Sachs-Platz. It has served as the seat of the Israelitische Kultusgemeinde Nürnberg since the congregation gave up its previous postwar synagogue on Essenweinstraße, and forms part of a complex that includes a retirement home and community center, expanded in 2016 with a new hall named for longtime community chairman Arno Hamburger. The synagogue preserves the 'Judenstein', a medieval Torah shrine ornament salvaged from earlier Nuremberg synagogues before their destruction.
